title: SWAG covariance subspace to Mirror posterior coordinates
hypothesis: A structured Mirror coordinate over shared posterior mean and low-rank covariance preserves predictive NLL and calibration with fewer bytes than full covariance and improves over native SWAG/rank-1 BNN controls.
physical_object: one posterior mean and shared covariance representation
mirror_coordinate: sampled latent m mapped through low-rank covariance basis and diagonal correction
logical_multiplicity: posterior predictive function samples from one parameter state

development.selection_metric: predictive NLL, 90% interval coverage, actual serialized posterior bytes

fresh.reason: no audit if exact native SWAG alias appears

success_gate: NLL within .02 nat/example and 90% coverage within .03 of dense reference; >=25% fewer bytes than dense; better frontier than matched SWAG and rank-1 BNN.
failure_gate: Any quality/storage gate miss or exact SWAG/Mirror function and payload alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: No neural network, natural benchmark, optimizer training, fresh/audit or deployment claim.
This tests posterior representation, not independent model capacity.
